children: The proposed Odisha project is expected to add 5 million tonnes of annual steel capacity, subject to regulatory approvals for the merger

Tata Steel is targeting the completion of its merger with Neelachal Ispat Nigam (NINL) by the end of March 2027, ahead of a proposed Rs 40,000 crore expansion of the steelmaker’s plant in Odisha. The merger remains on track for completion in the current financial year, subject to final approval from the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Tata Steel Executive Director and Chief Financial Officer Koushik Chatterjee said.

The NCLT’s Cuttack Bench is scheduled to hear the matter later in November 2026. The proposed amalgamation would bring NINL, which is already a wholly owned subsidiary of Tata Steel, directly into the parent company.

Tata Steel’s board approved the amalgamation scheme in March 2026. The NCLT issued an order on the first application in August, with the next hearing expected to address the final approval required to complete the merger.

Tata Steel acquired control of NINL in July 2022 through its then subsidiary Tata Steel Long Products, purchasing a 93.71 per cent stake for Rs 12,100 crore under the government’s strategic disinvestment process. The company subsequently acquired the remaining minority interests and completed its acquisition of 100 per cent of NINL’s equity in July 2025.

Tata Steel Chief Executive and Managing Director T. V. Narendran said the proposed investment would increase NINL’s annual steel capacity by around 5 million tonnes. The plant currently has an annual capacity of approximately 1 million tonnes.

The expansion is focused on long steel products and envisages four rolling mills, including facilities for reinforcing bars and wire rods. NINL’s plant is located at Duburi in Odisha’s Jajpur district, around 5–10 kilometres from Tata Steel’s existing Kalinganagar facility.

NINL’s operations include iron ore mining and processing, pig iron and long steel production, alongside a coke oven plant and a captive power plant. The proximity of the two facilities offers scope for sharing infrastructure and resources.

The proposed investment follows Tata Steel’s separate Rs 27,000 crore expansion at Kalinganagar, inaugurated in May 2025. The project increased the facility’s annual crude steel capacity from 3 million tonnes to 8 million tonnes.

The NINL expansion would add long-product capacity to the wider Kalinganagar industrial cluster, complementing operations that supply steel grades for sectors such as automotive, infrastructure and shipbuilding.

The merger and proposed capacity addition form part of Tata Steel’s plans to consolidate its Odisha operations and expand its steelmaking footprint. Completion of the amalgamation remains dependent on the tribunal’s final approval, while the proposed expansion is expected to increase NINL’s production capacity substantially.
